# J9 — Make the DC transport actually drive a writing reconcile pass

## Context / Problem

Story J7 [rebar:b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1] landed the DC backend's port conformance and made it reachable
through config, then drove it against a REAL Jira Data Center instance for the first time (GitHub
Actions run 30604756524). The writing path CRASHES:

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: 'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute
    'set_entity_property'

`--mode dry-run` passes; `--mode bootstrap-strict` exits 1. So epic e369's headline capability —
Jira Server/Data Center support — does not work yet, and the epic cannot honestly close without this.

Filed as [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5]; this story is its implementation.

## The root cause is a PORT defect, and the gap is TWELVE members

An AST audit over `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/*.py` — collecting every method invoked on a
`client`/`transport` receiver, diffed against `JiraDataCenterTransport`'s methods and against every
Protocol in `_backend.py` — measured the real gap:

**Called by the core, ABSENT from the DC transport (12):**
`delete_issue`, `delete_issue_link`, `get_comments`, `get_issue_by_rest`, `get_issue_links`,
`get_parent_map`, `remove_label`, `set_entity_property`, `set_issue_property`, `set_parent`,
`set_reporter`, `validate_assignee_exists`.

**Declared on NO Protocol in `_backend.py`: the same 12.**

**The dominant failure mode is SILENT DEGRADATION, not crashing** — which inverts the obvious framing
of this story. Classifying every call site by whether an enclosing `try` swallows `Exception`:

| behaviour | count | members |
|---|---|---|
| propagates (crashes) | 2 | `get_issue_by_rest`, `set_reporter` |
| swallowed at EVERY site | 7 | `delete_issue_link`, `get_comments`, `get_issue_links`, `set_issue_property`, `set_parent`, `validate_assignee_exists`, `get_parent_map` (the last via `hasattr`, `fetcher.py:448`) |
| MIXED — crashes at some sites, swallowed at others | 3 | `delete_issue`, `remove_label`, `set_entity_property` |

So a DC deployment does not mostly crash: it mostly **appears to converge while quietly not syncing
comments, links, parents, issue properties, or validating assignees.** `set_entity_property` is
swallowed at 2 of its 3 sites and crashes at the third — which is the ONLY reason any of this was
discovered. The crash was the lucky case.

This has a direct consequence for the acceptance bar: "no `AttributeError`" is the WRONG criterion,
because it is already true at most sites and true for the wrong reason. Fixing only the crash would
produce a green live run with the silent gaps fully intact — a worse outcome than today, because the
green run would be taken as proof the capability works.

### Per-method triage is required — a blanket rule is wrong

Three of the twelve need a decision that "implement it like Cloud does" actively gets WRONG. Each was
verified in source, and they establish that this story is TRIAGE, not bulk translation:

* **`get_parent_map` — Cloud's implementation is NOT portable.** `acli_graph.py:180` uses
  `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` with an opaque `nextPageToken` CURSOR, and its own docstring records
  (ticket 8b25, live-proven) that the legacy `/rest/api/3/search` is RETIRED with HTTP 410 and that
  **sending `startAt` is rejected with HTTP 400**. That endpoint and pagination model are Cloud-v3
  only. DC REST v2 has `POST /rest/api/2/search` with OFFSET paging (`startAt`/`maxResults`). So the
  Approach's "read each Cloud counterpart first" is actively misleading here: copying Cloud yields a
  404/400 against DC. This one needs a v2 offset-paged implementation written fresh.
* **`set_reporter` is UNREACHABLE on DC as the code stands.** Its only call site,
  `dispatch_apply_phases._update_one_apply_reporter`, resolves the reporter through
  `_jira_account_id_for` → `identity.jira_account_id`, and on `None` records an
  `outbound-reporter-unresolved` alert and RETURNS — before `client.set_reporter` is ever invoked.
  DC has no accountIds at all (`NameIdentity` keys on `name`), so that resolution misses and the
  transport method is never called. Implementing it on the DC transport alone would be DEAD CODE.
  The real decision is upstream: teach the call site DC's name-based identity, or record reporter
  sync as explicitly unsupported on DC. Either is defensible; silently adding an unreachable method
  is not.
* **`set_entity_property`** is the one with live evidence, and it is the story's spine — but note it
  is swallowed at 2 of its 3 sites, so fixing it does NOT make the other two observable.

### The triage, DECIDED — verdict per member

Recorded here so the executor implements rather than researches. Each verdict is backed by the call
site and by DC REST **v2** (not Cloud v3). "IMPLEMENT" means a normal v2 call; the two hard cases are
called out explicitly.

| member | verdict | basis |
|---|---|---|
| `set_entity_property` | IMPLEMENT | `PUT /rest/api/2/issue/{key}/properties/{prop}`, value PUT **verbatim** as the body (Cloud bug 0b27: wrapping it in `{"value": …}` silently stored the wrong shape) |
| `set_issue_property` | IMPLEMENT | same endpoint — Cloud's `set_entity_property` is literally an alias of it (`acli_rest.py:266`) |
| `delete_issue` | IMPLEMENT | `DELETE /rest/api/2/issue/{key}` |
| `delete_issue_link` | IMPLEMENT | `DELETE /rest/api/2/issueLink/{linkId}` |
| `get_comments` | IMPLEMENT | `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{key}/comment` — the DC transport already has `get_comment_map`, so the shape is established |
| `get_issue_by_rest` | IMPLEMENT | `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{key}`, returning the RAW dict (the DC transport's existing contract: never leak a `jira.Issue`) |
| `get_issue_links` | IMPLEMENT | read `issuelinks` off the issue fields; `JiraDataCenterBackend.map_remote_links` already canonicalizes that exact shape |
| `remove_label` | IMPLEMENT | `PUT /rest/api/2/issue/{key}` with `update.labels: [{"remove": <label>}]` — mirrors the existing `add_label` |
| `validate_assignee_exists` | IMPLEMENT — **not** `NotImplementedError` | `outbound_assignee.py:107-115` branches on `type(exc).__name__ == "AssigneeNotFoundError"`: that exact type ALREADY EXISTS in the DC transport (`transport.py:43`, subclassing `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError`) and is already raised by `_assign`. A `NotImplementedError` would fall to the `(None, False, False)` non-authoritative branch on EVERY DC assignee resolution — a permanent silent degradation to string-matching. Implement via DC's `GET /rest/api/2/user?username=`, raising the existing `AssigneeNotFoundError` on a definitive miss |
| `get_parent_map` | IMPLEMENT, v2 shape ONLY | `POST /rest/api/2/search` with OFFSET paging (`startAt`/`maxResults`). Do **not** port Cloud's `/rest/api/3/search/jql` cursor loop — its own docstring records that `startAt` is rejected there with HTTP 400 |
| `set_parent` | **SPIKE FIRST — the one genuine unknown** | On DC, a SUB-TASK's parent is `fields.parent`, but EPIC membership is the "Epic Link" **custom field** (`customfield_NNNNN`, instance-specific), not `parent`. rebar models epics as ordinary parents, so a naive `fields.parent` write may silently no-op for epic links. Resolve against the J5 harness before implementing; if the custom-field id cannot be discovered reliably, `NotImplementedError` naming the epic-link limitation is the honest outcome |
| `set_reporter` | UNREACHABLE-BY-CALL-SITE — upstream decision | never invoked on DC (see triage above). Either teach `dispatch_apply_phases._update_one_apply_reporter` DC's name identity, or record reporter sync as unsupported on DC. A transport method alone is dead code |

**Collateral finding, worth its own note:** `outbound_assignee.py:113` classifies by
`type(exc).__name__ == "AssigneeNotFoundError"` — a STRING comparison on a class name, not an
`isinstance` against the vendor-neutral `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` that both adapters already
subclass. It works, but it silently breaks on any rename and bypasses the neutral base class that
exists precisely for this. Flag it; fixing it is optional here and should not expand this story.

So each of the twelve needs a recorded verdict — IMPLEMENT (with the DC v2 shape, not Cloud's),
NOT-APPLICABLE (`NotImplementedError` naming the limitation), or UNREACHABLE-BY-CALL-SITE (with the
upstream decision named) — backed by the call-site evidence, not by symmetry with Cloud.

A METHODOLOGICAL NOTE, because it changed the answer twice: an audit that matches only
`client.method(...)` CALL forms under-counts, because the reconciler frequently passes the method as
a VALUE — `_call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)` (`dispatch_one.py:731`),
`_call_with_retry(client.set_entity_property, ...)` (`dispatch_one.py:321`). The audit must collect
every ATTRIBUTE ACCESS on a `client`/`transport` receiver. A first pass using the narrow pattern
reported ten and missed `delete_issue_link` and `set_parent`; the corrected pass reports twelve.

All twelve ARE implemented for Cloud, spread across `adapters/jira/acli_rest.py`, `acli.py` and
`acli_graph.py`.

So `set_entity_property` is not "the" missing method — it is the FIRST one a live writing pass
happened to reach. Eleven more sit behind it. **Implementing only `set_entity_property` would move the
crash one call deeper** and produce another red run, looking like progress while the capability stays
broken.

`TicketTransport` declares six members (`create_issue`, `get_issue`, `update_issue`,
`transition_issue_by_name`, `add_label`, `search_issues`); the core reaches for twenty-one distinct
transport members. The port describes under a third of its own requirement. That is exactly why `isinstance` conformance, the backend contract suite,
and 1636 reconciler unit tests were all green against a transport that cannot complete a writing pass.
**Conformance to an incomplete port proves less than it appears to** — the same class as J6's
`add_label` defect, where the only oracle was a fake mirroring the author's assumption.

## Approach

1. TRIAGE each of the twelve to one of IMPLEMENT / NOT-APPLICABLE / UNREACHABLE-BY-CALL-SITE, with
   evidence (see the triage section above — `get_parent_map` and `set_reporter` both break the naive
   rule). Then implement the IMPLEMENT set against DC's REST **v2** API. Read each Cloud counterpart
   for its CONTRACT, but do not assume its endpoint or pagination is portable — `set_entity_property` is
   Cloud's alias for `set_issue_property`, which PUTs to
   `/rest/api/3/issue/{key}/properties/{prop}` with the value sent **verbatim as the body** — an
   earlier Cloud bug (0b27) wrapped it in `{"value": ...}` and silently stored the wrong shape, so
   copy the corrected contract, not the intuition. DC is REST **v2**.
2. Where a method is genuinely not applicable to DC, it must raise a clear `NotImplementedError`
   naming the DC limitation — never be left absent to fail as `AttributeError` mid-pass. Each such
   decision needs evidence, not assumption.
3. Make absence detectable AT CONSTRUCTION rather than at some call site months later. `TicketTransport`
   is currently `class TicketTransport(Protocol)` with **no `@runtime_checkable`**, so
   `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` raises `TypeError` rather than returning `False` — verified
   directly, and it means the naive "just isinstance it" mechanism does not work. So: add
   `@runtime_checkable` to `TicketTransport` (matching `Backend` and the capability protocols, which
   already carry it), declare the required members on it, and assert conformance where a backend is
   BUILT — `_build_jira_datacenter_backend` in `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` and the Cloud
   equivalent — so a missing member fails loudly at construction.
4. Add a STRUCTURAL TEST that every transport member the core reaches for is declared on the port.
   It must collect EVERY attribute access on a `client`/`transport` receiver, not just call forms:
   a call-form-only audit silently under-counts (see the methodological note below) and would let the
   thirteenth member slip in unnoticed. This is what stops the class of defect recurring on the next
   backend.

**Alternative rejected:** implement `set_entity_property` alone. It fixes one crash, leaves eleven,
and leaves the port still misdescribing what the core needs.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — implement (or
  explicitly `NotImplementedError`) the ELEVEN unguarded absentees listed in the audit above, plus a
  deliberate decision on `get_parent_map`. **NOT just `set_entity_property`** — implementing one
  method moves the crash one call deeper and produces another red live run.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — add `@runtime_checkable` to `TicketTransport`
  (it currently lacks it, so `isinstance` against it raises `TypeError`) and declare the members the
  core actually requires.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py` — ONLY if the `set_reporter` verdict
  is resolved by teaching the call site DC's name-based identity (the alternative, recording reporter
  sync as unsupported on DC, touches no code here). Scoped because the triage permits that option.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` and
  `adapters/jira/backend.py` — assert transport conformance in the FACTORY, where the backend is
  built, so a missing member fails loudly at construction rather than at a call site later.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py` — `FakeTransport` gains whatever members the
  widened port declares, since it is the contract suite's stand-in and must satisfy it.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — a structural test for the audit: every transport attribute the
  core reaches for is declared on the Protocol.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` — already written by J7; it is the oracle and
  must go from FAIL to PASS unmodified. **Do not weaken it to accommodate the fix.**

## Testing

- unit: each implemented method issues the right REST call, asserted against a fake client. For
  `set_entity_property` this includes
  that the property KEY and VALUE reach the endpoint intact, since a silently wrong shape breaks
  correlation without raising.
- structural: the core-call-sites-vs-Protocol audit is a TEST, not a one-off grep, so a future core
  module reaching for an undeclared transport method fails CI. Give it teeth with a synthetic case,
  mirroring `test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py::test_checker_flags_a_synthetic_violation`.
- live: J7's `test_reconcile_pass.py` must pass in the `jira-dc-harness` CI job.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ALL TWELVE absent members carry a RECORDED VERDICT — implemented, `NotImplementedError` naming
      the DC limitation, or documented as unreachable-by-call-site with the upstream decision named —
      never simply absent: `delete_issue`, `delete_issue_link`, `get_comments`, `get_issue_by_rest`,
      `get_issue_links`, `get_parent_map`, `remove_label`, `set_entity_property`,
      `set_issue_property`, `set_parent`, `set_reporter`, `validate_assignee_exists`
- [ ] the acceptance bar is NOT "no `AttributeError`". For each of the SEVEN members whose call sites
      swallow `Exception` at every site, and the THREE mixed ones, a test asserts the member is
      actually PRESENT on the transport — because absence at those sites produces silent degradation,
      so "the pass converged" and "no exception escaped" are both true today while nothing works
- [ ] a test asserts a DC transport with a member REMOVED is rejected at construction (not at a later
      call site), proving the guard fires
- [ ] `get_parent_map` is implemented against DC REST **v2** offset pagination
      (`POST /rest/api/2/search`, `startAt`/`maxResults`) or explicitly declined — NOT copied from
      Cloud, whose `/rest/api/3/search/jql` cursor endpoint rejects `startAt` with HTTP 400 and does
      not exist on DC
- [ ] `set_reporter` gets an upstream decision, not just a transport method: either
      `_update_one_apply_reporter` is taught DC's name-based identity, or reporter sync is recorded
      as unsupported on DC — a transport method alone is unreachable dead code, asserted by a test
      that the call site is or is not reached
- [ ] `set_entity_property` specifically is implemented and unit-tested, with the test asserting the
      property key and value reach the REST layer INTACT — Cloud bug 0b27 stored `{"value": x}`
      instead of `x`, and a wrong shape breaks correlation WITHOUT raising, so "it did not error" is
      not evidence here
- [ ] `TicketTransport` is made `@runtime_checkable` and declares the members the core requires —
      without that decorator `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` raises `TypeError` rather than
      returning `False` (verified), so the construction-time guard cannot work at all as a bare
      isinstance check
- [ ] the conformance assertion runs where a backend is BUILT (`_build_jira_datacenter_backend` and
      the Cloud equivalent), so a missing member is a loud construction failure
- [ ] a structural test asserts every transport member the core reaches for is declared on the port,
      collecting EVERY attribute access on a `client`/`transport` receiver — not just `client.x(...)`
      call forms, since a call-form-only audit silently under-counts (it missed `delete_issue_link`
      and `set_parent` here). Proven to FIRE on a synthetic undeclared member
- [ ] [operator-attested] a full writing reconcile pass (`bootstrap-strict`) against the J5 harness converges with no
      unhandled exception — J7's `test_dc_reconcile_pass_raises_no_unhandled_exception` passes for a
      WRITING mode, not only dry-run
- [ ] [operator-attested] an immediately repeated writing pass writes nothing (idempotence) —
      J7's `test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` passes
- [ ] [operator-attested] a DC-created ticket carries `creation_channel == 'jira'` — J7's
      `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` passes
- [ ] the three live tests above pass WITHOUT any edit to `test_reconcile_pass.py` (`git diff` shows
      that file unchanged) — the oracle is not adjusted to fit the fix

## Note on the moved criteria

The three `[operator-attested]` live criteria were J7's. They are relocated here, not dropped: J7
cannot satisfy them (its own scope is landed and verified), and this is the story whose fix makes them
passable. Epic e369 therefore still requires a proven live writing pass before it closes.
